knowledge_point.title: Integrating a Quotient of Trigonometric Functions Using Trigonometric Identities

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=3x$, so $\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u$. Apply the constant multiple rule to take $1/3$ outside the integral. For the remaining integral, we have:

We can write the integral as

$$
\int \frac{{tan}^{2}⁡u-{sin}^{3}⁡u}{{sin}^{2}⁡u}\,\teut{d}u=\int \frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡u}({tan}^{2}⁡u-{sin}^{3}⁡u)\teut{d}u.
$$

We then use the fact that ${tan}^{2}⁡u=\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡u}{{cos}^{2}⁡u}$ to eupress this as

$$
\int \frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡u}(\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡u}{{cos}^{2}⁡u}-{sin}^{3}⁡u)\teut{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{tan}^{2}⁡u-{sin}^{3}⁡u}{{sin}^{2}⁡u}\,\teut{d}u & =\int \frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡u}(\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡u}{{cos}^{2}⁡u}-{sin}^{3}⁡u)\teut{d}u \\  & =\int (\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡u}\cdot \frac{{sin}^{2}⁡u}{{cos}^{2}⁡u}-\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡u}\cdot {sin}^{3}⁡u)\teut{d}u \\  & =\int (\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡u}-\operatorname{sin}⁡u)\teut{d}u \\  & =\int ({sec}^{2}⁡u-\operatorname{sin}⁡u)\teut{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡u-(-\operatorname{cos}⁡u)+C \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡u+\operatorname{cos}⁡u+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying this result by $1/3$ and substituting back $u=3x$, we obtain

$$
\int \frac{- \sin^{3}{\left(3 x \right)} + \tan^{2}{\left(3 x \right)}}{\sin^{2}{\left(3 x \right)}}\,\text{d}x=C + \frac{\cos{\left(3 x \right)}}{3} + \frac{\tan{\left(3 x \right)}}{3}.
$$

generation.domain: Real x on each connected interval where the original quotient at r*x is defined; removable lower endpoint for cot/csc definite templates uses its continuous limit.
generation.recipe_policy: Complete original bank transported by v(x)->v(r*x)/r; C remains arbitrary. No pooled or invented distractors.
